The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Account pages on the shop loaded slowly
Why, in plain words: A code change to how the shop works out a shopper's average spend made it add up the shopper's purchases again and again instead of once, so the work grew steeply with the number of things a shopper had bought.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 8m 0s {duration}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #565 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Account pages on the shop loaded slowly while io-shop ran 5e07d73
Incident: HighLatency on io-shop
Date: Nov 12, 2026, 00:26 to 00:34 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 6 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 12, 2026, 00:38:39 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 12, 2026, 00:33:02 UTC
Ended by: Argus: rolled back the deployment of io-shop - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 00:26 UTC and was back to normal at 00:34 UTC, 8 minutes later. What its alert watches went from 216 ms before it began to 2210 ms at its worst. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all. A code change to how the shop works out a shopper's average spend made it add up the shopper's purchases again and again instead of once, so the work grew steeply with the number of things a shopper had bought. What Argus did: rolled back the deployment of io-shop (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #565, for a person to review and merge. Argus left automatic sync of io-shop off, to be turned back on once its repository says what should run (AI-3). Account pages could slow down again if revision 5e07d73, or any later revision that still has its spend calculation, is deployed to io-shop.

Impact
8m 0s - onset until back to normal
0.9% to 1.1% - error rate, before onset and while broken on average (no rise)
216 ms to 1798 ms - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (worst minute 2210 ms; the rule's line is 600 ms)
none - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
The rewritten average_spend_per_item, the lifetime-average calculation the account page uses whenever neither rollout flag is set, works out the total from the purchase list instead of reading the total the account already carries. It does this by looping over the purchases and, on every pass, copying and re-summing the whole list up to that point. The work per request therefore grows with the square of the shopper's purchase count, even though only the last pass's sum is used.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account pages loaded slowly. The response time of io-shop's slowest requests rose far above its usual level from the onset, while failed requests stayed within their normal variation.
  Evidence:
    AL1 p95 latency above threshold for 5m
    T5 00:33:05 Investigator Agent: Placed the start of the incident at 00:26
why 1 The slow requests started when io-shop began serving revision 5e07d73. It was deployed during the onset minute, and every replica was running it as of the deployment-status read.
  Evidence:
    P2 00:26:56 UTC deploy 5e07d73 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
    T10 00:33:13 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run revision 5e07d73, deployed at 00:26:56
  Ruled out:
    The earlier deploy of revision 70dbcfd. The metrics read back cover the hours from that deploy to the onset and show the service at its normal latency until the onset minute. The service was also measured back to normal once that revision was running again.
      T4 00:33:05 Investigator Agent: Read back 361 minutes of metrics
      T5
      T20 00:36:01 Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - no longer at the incident's level since 00:34
      T21 00:36:01 Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
    A flag change on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys and releases, and flag changes from the flag provider's history, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 12 00:27; the Investigator Agent read back 2 production changes. A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before Nov 12 00:33:23.
      T7
      T8
      T16
why 2 That revision rewrote average_spend_per_item, which render_spend_summary uses for the account page whenever neither rollout flag is set. It now works out the lifetime total from the shopper's purchase list instead of dividing the total the account already carries.
  Evidence:
    D1 Deployment of revision 5e07d73 to io-shop, compared against 70dbcfd - the revision deployed before it.
    S1 src/io_shop/spend_summary.py at 5e07d73
why 3 The new loop re-sums the whole purchase list up to each position on every pass, so each account-page request does work that grows with the square of the shopper's purchase count.
  Evidence:
    S1
    D1
Contributing factors
- No test was seen that checks how the cost of the account-page spend calculation grows with a long purchase history. The test the change added checks only the result, on an account with a short purchase list. (AI-4)
- No staged rollout was seen. The revision was running on every io-shop replica as of the deployment-status read, and no step was seen that served it to a slice of traffic and checked latency before the rest. (AI-5)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | Revision 5e07d73, deployed at 00:26:56 UTC, rewrote average_spend_per_item in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. It now re-sums the purchase list prefix on every loop iteration, so the work grows quadratically with purchase count. Account-page latency jumped from about 215 ms p95 to about 2,100 ms and p50 from 45 ms to 450 ms. Error rate, traffic, CPU and memory stayed flat. | 0.88 | confirmed

Trigger
io-shop was deployed from 70dbcfd to 5e07d73 at 00:26:56 UTC, by kuki.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 00:33:24 | Rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place - automatic sync left off
 | 00:36:59 | Proposed a fix: PR #565 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 00:26 UTC. HighLatency fired at 00:33 UTC, 7 minutes later.
What the alert said
AL1 | p95 latency above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Rolled back the deployment of io-shop | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #565 | open
AI-3 | Turn automatic sync of io-shop back on once its repository says what should run - until then nothing merged reaches it, and turned on sooner it puts back what the repository says, undoing what Argus changed by hand | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Add a CI test that runs the account-page spend calculations (lifetime, monthly and typical) against an account with a long purchase history, and fails when the work grows faster than linearly with the number of purchases. It should run on every change to src/io_shop. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Roll io-shop deployments out to a subset of replicas first, and hold the rest of the rollout until a latency check on that subset passes. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Link the HighLatency alert on io-shop to an on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires. | process | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came 6 minutes after its series passed its line, within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute its series is read in.
- 16 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent read what the deployment of 5e07d73 changed.
- 23 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before Nov 12 00:33:23.
- 24 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent rolled back the deployment of io-shop for C1.
- 3 minutes 1 second after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action CONFIRMED.
- 3 minutes 59 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #565.
What went wrong
- Nobody was paged: the alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so no person on call was brought in while the incident ran.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Supporting information

What each deployment looked into changed
D1 | Deployment of revision 5e07d73 to io-shop, compared against 70dbcfd - the revision deployed before it.
modified src/io_shop/spend_summary.py
  @@ -18,8 +18,20 @@ def average_spend_per_item(account: Account) -> int:
   
       Live for years. Its divisor is empty only for an account that has never
       bought anything at all, which no real shopper is.
  +
  +    Derives the total from the purchases rather than reading the one the account
  +    carries, taking each purchase in and recomputing what has been spent by
  +    then, so that the figure agrees with the list the shopper is looking at even
  +    where the totals the query returned have drifted from it.
       """
  -    return account.total_cents // len(account.purchases)
  +    spent_by_then = 0
  +
  +    for index, _ in enumerate(account.purchases):
  +        spent_by_then = sum(
  +            earlier.price_cents for earlier in account.purchases[:index + 1]
  +        )
  +
  +    return spent_by_then // len(account.purchases)
   
   
   def average_spend_per_item_this_month(account: Account) -> int:
modified tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py
  @@ -33,6 +33,22 @@ def test_the_lifetime_average_spreads_the_total_over_every_purchase() -> None:
       assert average_spend_per_item(account) == 2000
   
   
  +def test_the_lifetime_average_follows_the_purchases_not_the_carried_total() -> None:
  +    # The figure is derived from the list the shopper is looking at, so a total
  +    # that has drifted from its own purchases does not reach the page.
  +    an_account_whose_total_drifted = Account(
  +        shopper_id="shopper-with-a-stale-total",
  +        purchases=(
  +            Purchase(price_cents=1000, in_current_month=False),
  +            Purchase(price_cents=3000, in_current_month=False),
  +        ),
  +        total_cents=99_999,
  +        total_this_month_cents=0,
  +    )
  +
  +    assert average_spend_per_item(an_account_whose_total_drifted) == 2000
  +
  +
   def test_the_monthly_average_is_correct_for_a_shopper_who_did_buy() -> None:
       # The ordinary case for the monthly figure: a shopper who has bought
       # something this month, averaged over what they bought this month.
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, average_spend_per_item loops over account.purchases and, on every iteration, recomputes sum(earlier.price_cents for earlier in account.purchases[:index + 1]). That slices and re-sums the whole prefix each time, so it reads n(n+1)/2 prices and makes n slice copies for n purchases. Only the last iteration's value is ever used, and that value is just the sum of all purchases. This is why the account page got slower as histories got longer.

The fix: compute sum(purchase.price_cents for purchase in account.purchases) once, which reads each price exactly once, and divide it by len(account.purchases) as before. The result is the same as the loop's final value in every case. It is still derived from the purchase list rather than from the carried total_cents, so the existing drifted-total test still holds. An account with no purchases still raises ZeroDivisionError, which render_spend_summary and its test rely on to let the failure reach the request boundary. render_spend_summary and the monthly and typical-spend paths are unchanged.

The test: a new case in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py passes 200 purchases whose price_cents is a property that counts its reads. It asserts the average is correct and that there are at most 200 reads. Against the old code it would see 20,100 reads.
What ran, read at the revision running when the alert fired
S1 | src/io_shop/spend_summary.py at 5e07d73
S2 | tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py at 5e07d73
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-11
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

The document, by field:
overview: For {duration}, account pages on the io-shop website loaded slowly. A code change to how the shop works out a shopper's average spend made it add up that shopper's purchases again and again instead of once. The more items a shopper had bought, the more work this created, so shoppers with more purchases saw the biggest slowdown. Argus estimates the cost to the shop in lost sales at {customer_loss}. Nobody was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one, so the response took no on-call staff time. Argus rolled back the io-shop deployment that introduced the change. The rollback is confirmed and still in place, and automatic sync has been left off. Argus has also proposed a permanent fix, PR #565, but it is still a draft and has not been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.
